title: Plok!
subtitle: Software Creations · Super Nintendo Entertainment System
summary: Plok! is Software Creations' Super Nintendo platformer about the red-hooded ruler of Akrillic defending his island from invading fleas. Plok can launch his arms and legs at enemies, waiting for each limb to return before using it again. The premise gives a colourful mascot an immediately unusual action. body: Plok! is Software Creations' Super Nintendo platformer about the red-hooded ruler of Akrillic defending his island from invading fleas. Plok can launch his arms and legs at enemies, waiting for each limb to return before using it again. The premise gives a colourful mascot an immediately unusual action. His own body supplies the weapons, so a missed shot changes what is available for the next encounter. The player crosses a bright island whose enemies and obstacles repeatedly find another use for that detachable anatomy.

Some targets require a limb to remain on a hanger after striking them, making activation a temporary sacrifice rather than a free action. Losing access to arms or legs changes how Plok can continue, with a limbless hero reduced to bouncing. A route has to be considered in relation to what will remain available after the switch is triggered. Presents and other power-ups add further variations, allowing the game to move between ordinary platforming and sections built around another temporary set of tools.

Ste and John Pickford began the idea as Fleapit, an unrealised arcade project developed while they worked at Zippo Games. It later became a Software Creations production for the Super Nintendo, released in 1993. Tim and Geoff Follin's score gives the stages a particularly energetic musical identity. The finished game belongs to the crowded age of mascot platformers, but its central gesture remains specific: Plok attacks by sending away pieces of himself, and the interval before their return keeps changing the next available action.
story_headings: A hero whose limbs are ammunition
A switch can keep the limb
A long route from the arcade
